trends.what: A curated, community-maintained list of free public APIs for developers to use in their projects.
trends.why: It's the go-to reference for developers looking to quickly find and integrate third-party services, making it a perennial favorite for API discovery.

trends.what: An open-source platform offering free coding lessons, projects, and certifications in web development, data science, and more.
trends.why: It's a massive, self-paced learning resource that keeps growing, making it a top destination for anyone from beginners to career-changers.

trends.what: A massive collection of freely available programming books, tutorials, and learning resources in multiple languages.
trends.why: It democratizes access to technical knowledge, constantly updated by the community, making it a staple for self-taught developers.

trends.what: A cross-platform personal AI assistant that runs locally on any OS, designed to be your own private, always-available helper.
trends.why: It taps into the growing demand for private, self-hosted AI that doesn't rely on cloud services, appealing to privacy-conscious users.

trends.what: Interactive roadmaps and guides that outline step-by-step learning paths for various developer roles and technologies.
trends.why: It provides clear, visual career guidance in a field where the learning path is often overwhelming, making it a top bookmark for devs.

trends.what: A tool that makes AI agents generate minimal, lazy, and efficient code by mimicking the habits of a senior developer who avoids over-engineering.
trends.why: It's a humorous yet practical take on AI code generation, addressing the common problem of AI producing overly complex solutions.

trends.what: A fullscreen, mouse-interactive terminal UI (TUI) and harness for running coding agents, designed for extensibility and control.
trends.why: It brings a modern, interactive coding experience to the terminal, appealing to developers who prefer powerful CLI tools over IDEs.

trends.what: A pure C, zero-dependency runtime that runs large mixture-of-experts (MoE) AI models on consumer hardware by streaming experts from disk.
trends.why: It challenges the assumption that frontier AI needs expensive GPUs, making powerful models accessible on everyday machines.
